reasoning_trace.value: The paper includes several images, including a conceptual diagram of OCC spatial multiplexing, a system architecture diagram of the HP-OCC receiver, an application diagram of warehouse automation, and hardware photos of a passive transmitter tag and a portable HP-OCC receiver. These images provide visual evidence of the HP-OCC system's components and functionality.

The paper proposes High-Performance Optical Camera Communications (HP-OCC) as an alternative to RF-based ISAC. HP-OCC combines single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) sensors with on-sensor edge processing, enabling high-speed optical communication and centimeter-level localization. The system uses spatial multiplexing, where a camera sensor isolates signals from multiple transmitters, and each transmitter maps to a unique pixel region.

The paper reports a video rate of 5 Mbps and a localization accuracy of 10 cm at a range of 25 m. The system also demonstrates low packet loss and stable performance in a warehouse automation scenario. These results suggest that HP-OCC can achieve high-speed communication and accurate localization in a practical setting.

The paper highlights the advantages of HP-OCC over RF-based ISAC, including higher sensing precision, power efficiency, and environmental compatibility. However, it also notes the limitation of requiring line-of-sight between transmitters and receivers. Future work could investigate hybrid optical-RF ISAC approaches to mitigate this limitation.
